obj.location: the line `n /= 10` inside the while loop
obj.cause: In Python 3, `/=` is true division, so `n` becomes a float (123 -> 12.3 -> 1.23 ...) instead of shrinking by one integer digit. The loop then sums fractional remainders and never yields the integer digit sum 6.
obj.change: Replace `n /= 10` with integer division `n //= 10` so each step drops the last digit and `n` stays an int until it reaches 0.
obj.verification: Re-run `assert digits_sum(123) == 6`. Also check `digits_sum(0) == 0` and `digits_sum(-45) == 9` to confirm zeros and the abs() path still work.
